```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The question asks for a paying customer within 90 days. A has sourced evidence that this buyer pays: ClaireMed publishes $99/provider/month and S10.AI publishes $99–$500/provider/month. B's own brief says 'No clean single payer found' and that every named direct competitor is free to the end user.",
    "A's own failure case still shows the first-customer goal can be met. Cydoc, nearly the same product, reached four paying customers and $27,900 in 2024 revenue. B offers no example of any comparable product earning money from any payer except grants, VC, or nonprofit dues.",
    "A's main risks are cost and pace: $4–6k integration per practice, BAA/HIPAA overhead, and a slow custom sales cycle. These make scaling hard but do not rule out one paying customer. A proposes a narrower paste-into-existing-EHR layer, and the brief notes that psych reports produced most of Cydoc's actual revenue, which suggests a narrower wedge.",
    "B's backup payer path (municipal Vision Zero programs, research grants) has no source. B's own open questions ask whether cities or nonprofits would pay for a third-party tool at all. Grant and municipal procurement cycles also look poorly suited to a 90-day window, though the brief gives no evidence on this either way.",
    "B's distribution is also unproven. The CPI benchmark of $1–$5 per install is generic and says nothing about conversion to paid. The advocacy-partnership channel has no sourced sign of interest from any organization, and those organizations already run their own free tools."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence has no willingness-to-pay signal at all. It rests on a one-line Hacker News wish, copy from a free nonprofit reporting form, and a quote from a founder of another free app. None of these shows anyone paying, or offering to pay, for the product. Combined with 'No clean single payer found,' the payer case is effectively missing.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A's demand evidence is also thin: one Reddit complaint about intake paperwork, not about buying software, plus an AMA statistic relayed by a competitor. The 'apparent traction' of competitors in A's Case For has no source; only their published prices count. A's Case Against is a strong, sourced warning that the business may not be sustainable. I picked A because on the narrow test of landing one paying customer in 90 days, it has sourced evidence of willingness to pay and B has none."
}
```
